claim: Board of review meets the second Monday in March; a city or township may authorize alternative start dates of the Tuesday or Wednesday following.
Tax Tribunal petition deadline: May 31 of the tax year for commercial, industrial, developmental real property and commercial/industrial/utility personal property.
Tax Tribunal petition deadline: July 31 of the tax year for agricultural, residential, timber-cutover real property and agricultural personal property.
In all other tribunal matters, a petition must be filed within 35 days after the final decision, ruling, or determination.
Taxable value is the lesser of (a) prior-year taxable value minus losses times the lesser of 1.05 or the inflation rate, plus additions, or (b) current state equalized valuation (Proposal A cap).
On a transfer of ownership, taxable value for the following calendar year becomes the property's state equalized valuation (uncapping).
The buyer must notify the local assessing office of the transfer within 45 days on a State Tax Commission form (Property Transfer Affidavit).
Form 2766 Property Transfer Affidavit must be filed by the new owner with the city/township assessor within 45 days of transfer.

A principal residence is exempt from the tax levied by a local school district for school operating purposes if the owner files an affidavit.
For taxes levied after 2011, the affidavit is due on or before June 1 for the summer levy or on or before November 1 for the winter levy.
The exemption lasts until December 31 of the year the property is transferred or is no longer a principal residence.
An owner must rescind the exemption within 90 days after the property stops being the owner's principal residence; late rescission penalty is $5 per day up to $200.
An owner may retain the exemption up to 3 tax years on a former residence if it is not occupied, is for sale, not leased, and not used for business, by filing a conditional rescission form.
Form 2368 Principal Residence Exemption Affidavit is filed with the city/township assessor; deadlines June 1 (summer levy) and November 1 (winter levy).
A principal residence exemption exempts the home from local school operating millage, up to 18 mills.

State real estate transfer tax is $3.75 for each $500 or fraction of the total value of property transferred.
County real estate transfer tax is 55 cents per $500 in counties under 2,000,000 population; up to 75 cents per $500 in counties of 2,000,000 or more.
State transfer tax exempt: instruments with consideration under $100.
State transfer tax exempt: conveyance from an individual to the individual's child, stepchild, adopted child, or grandchild.
State transfer tax exempt: instruments transferring property pursuant to or in lieu of mortgage foreclosure (not a subsequent transfer by the foreclosing entity).
State transfer tax exempt: quitclaim deed to confirm title already vested/correct a flaw in title; judgments/orders of a court of record without specified monetary consideration.
County transfer tax exemptions include consideration under $100, leases, security instruments, court orders, boundary line instruments, and land contracts where legal title has not passed.
A mortgage containing a power of sale may be foreclosed by advertisement on default.
Notice is published once a week for 4 successive weeks in a newspaper in the county, and a copy posted on the premises within 15 days after first publication.
Redemption period: 6 months for residential property up to 4 units if the amount due exceeds 66-2/3% of original indebtedness, and for commercial/industrial/multifamily over 4 units.
Redemption period is 1 month if residential property (up to 4 units) is abandoned under MCL 600.3241; 30 days under 600.3241a.
Redemption period is 1 year for agricultural property or where other subsections do not apply.
Redemption amount is the bid, interest at the mortgage rate from the sale date, sheriff's fee paid by purchaser, plus $5 if paid to the register of deeds.
The former foreclosure-notice/loan-modification/housing-counselor provisions (MCL 600.3205a-3205d) were repealed effective June 30, 2013.

Foreclosure sale is a public sale between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m. at the place of holding circuit court in the county, conducted by the person named in the mortgage or the sheriff/undersheriff/deputy, to the highest bidder.
A purchaser's deed is void if the mortgagor or person with recorded interest redeems within the applicable period by paying the required amount.
The purchaser must record an affidavit stating the exact redemption amount; the redemption date is stated on the certificate of sale.
Court may order property turned over to surviving spouse or heirs without administration if the gross estate balance is $50,000 or less after funeral/burial expenses are shown paid.
Michigan Courts SCAO provides probate forms including Petition for Approval of Sale of Real Estate (Decedent Estate), filed in probate court.
